Q: WPF Application that only has a tray icon A:

I recently had this same problem. Unfortunately, NotifyIcon is only a Windows.Forms control at the moment, if you want to use it you are going to have to include that part of the framework. I guess that depends how much of a WPF purist you are.

If you want a quick and easy way of getting started check out this WPF NotifyIcon control on the Code Project which does not rely on the WinForms NotifyIcon at all. A more recent version seems to be available on the author's website and as a NuGet package. This seems like the best and cleanest way to me so far.

  • Rich ToolTips rather than text
  • WPF context menus and popups
  • Command support and routed events
  • Flexible data binding
  • Rich balloon messages rather than the default messages provides by the OS

Check it out. It comes with an amazing sample app too, very easy to use, and you can have great looking Windows Live Messenger style WPF popups, tooltips, and context menus. Perfect for displaying an RSS feed, I am using it for a similar purpose.

Q: Homebrew services. I can’t start the service and get "Bootstrap failed: 5: Input/output error" A:

This following worked for me.

Note: The path to my LaunchAgents, MongoDB, and log might be different from yours. Make sure to pass the correct path.

brew services cleanup
brew uninstall mongodb-community
brew install mongodb-community
brew services start mongodb-community

Stop and unload the launch agent completely

brew services stop mongodb-community
launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u) ~/Library/LaunchAgents/homebrew.mxcl.mongodb-community.plist

 Delete the old .plist file, so Homebrew (executable brew) regenerates it:

rm -f ~/Library/LaunchAgents/homebrew.mxcl.mongodb-community.plist

Ensure data and log directories exist and have the correct permissions

mkdir -p /opt/homebrew/var/mongodb
mkdir -p /opt/homebrew/var/log
sudo chown -R $(whoami) /opt/homebrew/var/mongodb /opt/homebrew/var/log

 Start manually to confirm MongoDB runs:

mongod --dbpath /opt/homebrew/var/mongodb

If it starts without errors here, we know the problem is only the launchctl integration.

Let Homebrew (executable brew) recreate and start the service:

brew services start mongodb-community

Q: proxychains does not work with browsers (chromium, firefox) but work with curl A:

you should make some settings on your browser. Go to firefox settings and then scroll down, you will se network settings, choose manuel proxy configuration, SOCKS Host: 127.0.0.1 and it's port to 9050 which will connect you to tor. and click to proxy dns when using socks4 and socks5 then save. that is the only way that worked for me.

Q: Azure Data factory - data flow expression date and timestamp conversions A:

  1. toDate() converts input date string to date with default format as yyyy-[M]M-[d]d. Accepted formats are :[ yyyy, yyyy-[M]M, yyyy-[M]M-[d]d, yyyy-[M]M-[d]dT* ].

    Same goes with toTimestamp(), the default pattern is yyyy-[M]M-[d]d hh:mm:ss[.f...] when it is used.

  2. In Azure SQL Database as well the default date and datetime2 formats are in YYYY-MM-DD and YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss as shown below.

  1. But if your column datatypes are in string (varchar) format, then you can change the output format of date and DateTime in azure data flow mappings.

When loaded to Azure SQL database, it is shown as below:

Note: This format results when datatype is varchar

  1. If the datatype is the date in the Azure SQL database, you can convert them to the required format using date conversions as

select id, col1, date1, convert(varchar(10),date1,105) as 'dd-MM-YYYY' from test1

  1. Azure SQL Database always follows the UTC time zone. Using “AT TIME ZONE” convert it another non-UTC time zone.

select getdate() as a, getdate() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AT TIME ZONE 'Central Standard Time' as b

You can also refer to sys.time_zone_info view to check current UTC offset information.

select * from sys.time_zone_info

Q: Run ansible-playbook with a user-data script on an EC2 instance A:

It does work, but you may face issues that it's not running. I solved it by adding a delay. The thing is, user data runs before many other dependencies finishes installation, thus ansible-playbook does not run. Adding a delay of 30 seconds solved it for me.

#!/bin/bash
cd /home/ubuntu
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install python3-pip -y
sudo pip3 install ansible
sleep 30
sudo ansible-playbook init.yml

I recommend use a longer sleep time first, then reduce it. See which works better for you. Best wishes.
